'''"Let Me In"''' is the name of a 1961 song with music and lyrics by [[The Sensations|Yvonne Baker]], recorded the same year by Baker and [[The Sensations]], which went to No. 2 on the US R&B singles chart and No. 4 on the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] singles chart. It reached number 5 in New Zealand on the lever hits parade chart.<ref>https://web.archive.org/web/20210208152417/http://www.flavourofnz.co.nz/index.php?qpageID=Lever%20hit%20parades&qyear=1962&qmonth=Apr&qweek=12-Apr-1962#n_view_location</ref> It was the group's highest charting and most successful single.<ref>{{cite book |title= Top R&B/Hip-Hop Singles: 1942-2004|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=516}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.45cat.com/artist/the-sensations-us|title=The Sensations [Philadelphia] Discography - USA - 45cat}}</ref>  "Let Me In" may be most memorable for its repetitive "weeoo" refrain in the chorus.

"Let Me In" is the name of a 1961 song with music and lyrics by Yvonne Baker, recorded the same year by Baker and The Sensations, which went to No. 2 on the US R&B singles chart and No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 singles chart. It reached number 5 in New Zealand on the lever hits parade chart. It was the group's highest charting and most successful single.  "Let Me In" may be most memorable for its repetitive "weeoo" refrain in the chorus.
